# Overview

&nbsp;

By streaming OCI image layers lazily over FUSE instead of downloading full layer tarballs upfront, `atelet` speeds up preparing actor root filesystems by 20+X while keeping Kubernetes and `containerd` CRI out of the actor critical path.

### Terminology

* **Agent Substrate & Actor (`atelet` / `ateom`):** Substrate multiplexes many mostly-idle agent workloads (**Actors**, analogous to lightweight **K8s Pods/containers**) onto pre-warmed K8s worker Pods without going through the K8s control plane or `containerd` CRI. On each node, **`atelet`** plays the role of **`kubelet` \+ `containerd` image manager** (resolving credentials and preparing OCI layers), while **`ateom`** plays the role of **`containerd-shim` \+ `runsc`** (assembling the `overlayfs` rootfs and running/restoring the Actor in `gVisor`).  
* **Provider:** The underlying image-streaming engine that FUSE-mounts OCI layers from a registry (e.g., Google Riptide, AWS SOCI, eStargz, Nydus).  
* **Adapter:** A lightweight DaemonSet plugin that serves as a bridge between Substrate and a specific streaming provider. It implements the `OCILayerService` gRPC API and talks to the specific streaming provider.

## Immediate-Term Proposal

**Goal:** Define Substrate's own `OCILayerService` gRPC API and ship functional end-to-end image streaming on GKE via a Riptide v2 Adapter DaemonSet.

&nbsp;

* **Core Substrate `OCILayerService` gRPC API:**  
  * Because CNCF's low-level `containerd.services.snapshots.v1.Snapshots` API lacks a standard credential-passing mechanism (`imagePullSecrets`), exposes a stateful `Active` to `Committed` snapshot-tree dance that `atelet` does not need (since `ateom` mounts the writable `overlayfs` upperdir), and exhibits provider-specific quirks across Riptide, SOCI, eStargz, and Nydus, Substrate defines its own higher-level `OCILayerService` gRPC service over a single Unix socket:  
    * `CanProvide(ctx, req) (bool, error)` — checks whether the provider can serve layers for the given OCI image (e.g., GAR eligibility check for Riptide).  
    * `PrepareLayers(ctx, req) (*PrepareLayersResponse, error)` — accepts the OCI image reference and optionally resolved registry credentials (`imagePullSecrets`), increments the per-image/per-layer reference count (`refCount`), and returns the complete ordered list of read-only host `LayerDirs` for the image.  
      * *All-or-Nothing Contract:* Strictly all-or-nothing per image—this choice gives a clear boundary (either `OCILayerService` returns all layers, or returns `ErrNotSupported` so `atelet` falls back to `imagecache` for the whole image), although it is technically possible for `atelet` to mix layers from streaming and `imagecache`. For providers like AWS SOCI that skip small layers, it is the adapter's responsibility to materialize those small layers internally and return the complete image.  
    * `ReleaseLayers(ctx, req) error` — decrements the per-image/per-layer reference count (`refCount`) on actor teardown or checkpoint and unmounts unused FUSE layer views when `refCount` reaches `0` (while preserving shared layers still referenced by other images/actors).  
    * `ReconcileLayers(ctx, active) error` — called by `atelet` on startup/restart with the list of active images/layers discovered from surviving on-disk actor bundle specs (`rootfs-overlay.json`), allowing the adapter to rebuild accurate in-memory `refCount`s and unmount any orphaned FUSE views left behind by an `atelet` crash.  
* **Out-of-Process Adapter DaemonSet Architecture:**  
  * Following the **Adapter pattern**—analogous to Kubernetes CSI (Container Storage Interface) drivers—each provider implements Substrate's uniform `OCILayerService` gRPC API as a standalone Go adapter deployed via a Kubernetes `DaemonSet` on worker nodes, translating Substrate's RPCs into the provider's native snapshotter protocol and auth sockets while keeping `atelet` 100% vendor-agnostic.  
  * **Repository Strategy:** To unblock v1, the Riptide adapter binary will initially live in a dedicated subfolder of the `substrate` repository, structured as a standalone component so it can move to an external plugins repository long-term.  
  * **Chunk Cache & Cross-Image Layer Deduplication:** The underlying provider (`gcfsd`) owns the node-level on-disk chunk cache; the adapter keys FUSE layer views by content-addressed `chainID`/`diffID` so shared layers across different OCI images reuse the same FUSE mount and chunk cache without streaming twice.  
* **Isolating from Host `containerd` GC via the DaemonSet:**  
  * When sharing the host Riptide Snapshotter and `gcfsd` daemon with Substrate, `containerd` GC interferences both via gRPC calls though they do not share any underlying DB. See *Appendix: [Host containerd GC Interferences](#host-containerd-gc-interferences)* for detailed explanation.  
  * DaemonSet Isolation:
    * The `riptide-provider` container runs an isolated `gcfsd` \+ `Riptide Snapshotter` pair (using the preloaded binaries) inside a child mount namespace (`unshare -m --propagation unchanged`), marks `/run` as `rslave`, bind-mounts `/run/ate-image-streaming/gcfsd` onto `/run/gcfsd` (satisfying `gcfsd-v2`'s hardcoded `/run/gcfsd/keychain.sock` path without touching the host's `/run/gcfsd`), and mounts FUSE at `/var/lib/substrate/gcfs/mnt` (`Bidirectional` propagation). This works identically on both GKE Nodes with Streaming Disabled and GKE Nodes with Streaming Enabled with zero interference.  
* **What Changes Across Components**  
  * **`atelet`:** Configured via a single flag: `--oci-layer-service-socket=<unix-socket-path>` (empty by default \= disabled; non-empty \= enabled). When applicable, resolves registry credentials via the Kubelet Credential Provider or workload `imagePullSecrets` and passes them inside `PrepareLayersRequest`.  
  * **`ateom`:** No protocol changes; mounts the `LayerDirs` listed in `rootfs-overlay.json` as read-only `overlayfs` `lowerdir` entries identically to locally unpacked layers.  
* **Separate On-Disk Folders & Dynamic Disabling**  
  * **Strict Directory Separation:** Locally unpacked layers, adapter streaming wrapper symlinks, and provider FUSE mounts / chunk caches live in completely separate directories on disk. See *Appendix: [On-Disk Folder Structure](#on-disk-folder-structure)* for details.  
  * **Avoiding Streaming Layers on Disable:** Unlike GKE `containerd` (where disabling Riptide leaves dangling `gcfs` snapshot metadata tied to image records), when streaming is dynamically disabled on a Substrate node:  
    1. **New & Resuming Actors:** `atelet` immediately stops routing new actors (`Run`) and resuming actors (`Restore`) to `/var/lib/ateom-gvisor/streaming/...` and instead pulls/unpacks layers into `/var/lib/ateom-gvisor/image-cache/layers/...`. Even an actor that was previously streaming seamlessly restores its checkpoint upperdir onto local `image-cache` layers on its next wakeup.  
    2. **Releasing & GC-ing Streamed Layers:** Already-running streamed actors continue uninterrupted; as each one checkpoints or terminates, its `refCount` decrements and once `refCount` reaches `0`, the `/var/lib/ateom-gvisor/streaming/...` wrapper directories and `/var/lib/substrate/gcfs` FUSE views are immediately unmounted and GC-ed.  
  * **Deployment Workflow:**  
    1. **Cluster Install (Disabled by Default, or Auto-Enabled with Flag):** `./hack/install-ate.sh --deploy-ate-system` deploys `atelet` without installing any adapter DaemonSet; adding `--setup-image-streaming=riptide` (or `ATE_OCILAYER_ADAPTER_MANIFEST=<path-or-url>` for out-of-tree adapters) installs the adapter DaemonSet, labels the nodes `ate.dev/oci-layer-service=riptide`, and automatically enables streaming across the cluster.  
    2. **Disable on a Node:** `kubectl label node <node> ate.dev/oci-layer-service=disabled --overwrite` keeps the adapter pod alive for currently running actors while `atelet` stops using streaming for new and resuming actors; once existing actors checkpoint or terminate, `refCount` reaches `0` and the streamed layers are GC-ed (re-enable anytime with `ate.dev/oci-layer-service=riptide`).
* **Upgrading the Adapter DaemonSet (Extending `atelet` Rolling Upgrades):**  
  * **Why In-Place FUSE Restarts Break Actors:** Stopping a userspace FUSE daemon (`gcfsd-v2` or `soci-snapshotter-grpc`) while an actor's `overlayfs` lowerdir is reading from `/dev/fuse` causes reads to fail with `ENOTCONN`.  
  * **Treating Adapter Upgrade as an `atelet` Dataplane Upgrade ([`docs/upgrade.md`](upgrade.md)):** Rather than introducing a separate upgrade mechanism, the Adapter DaemonSet follows `atelet`'s existing version-pinned rolling upgrade convention (`ate-ocilayer-<provider>-${SUBSTRATE_VERSION_SUFFIX}`), matching both `ate.dev/oci-layer-service: <provider>` and `ate.dev/substrate-version: "${SUBSTRATE_VERSION}"`:  
    1. **Side-by-Side Deployment:** Deploy `ate-ocilayer-<provider>-${NEW_SUFFIX}` alongside `atelet-${NEW_SUFFIX}` pinned to `$NEW_VERSION`. Both sit at `0` pods while nodes still carry `$OLD_VERSION`.  
    2. **Per-Node Worker Drain & Actor Suspend:** Following `docs/upgrade.md` Step 6a–6c, drain workers on `$NODE` (`DrainWorker`) and suspend all running actors on `$NODE`. Because suspending an actor triggers `Checkpoint` $\to$ `ReleaseLayers`, **zero running actors and zero active FUSE mounts remain on `$NODE`** once the drain completes.  
    3. **Shut Down Old Daemons, Then Cut Over to `$NEW_VERSION`:** Once `$NODE` has zero actors, removing the version label (`kubectl label node $NODE ate.dev/substrate-version-`) causes Kubernetes to terminate both the old `atelet` pod and the old `ate-ocilayer-<provider>` pod on `$NODE`. When the old adapter pod exits, its `ocilayer.sock`, BoltDB locks (`metadata.db` / `images_in_use.db`), and `/dev/fuse` mounts are all cleanly closed and released. Labeling the node with the new version (`kubectl label node $NODE ate.dev/substrate-version=$NEW_VERSION`) then starts the new `atelet` and new adapter pod on a clean node with zero contention. Rollback and retirement work identically.  
  * **Crash Isolation Between Upgrades:** Keeping the adapter in its own DaemonSet (rather than inside the `atelet` Pod) preserves `atelet`'s zero-capability security posture (`capabilities: drop: ["ALL"]`) and ensures that if `atelet` crashes and restarts in-place between upgrades, the FUSE daemon and active `/dev/fuse` mounts stay alive uninterrupted while `atelet` recovers state via `ReconcileLayers`.

## Medium-Term Proposal

* Optimize cold/warm latency after delivering functional Riptide v2  
* Extend to other OSS remote snapshotters  
* Dynamically disabling streaming

### Host `containerd` GC Interferences {#host-containerd-gc-interferences}

`containerd` GC interferences Substrate when it shares on-host Riptide Snapshotter and gcfsd.

&nbsp;

&nbsp;`containerd` and Riptide Snapshotter maintain two completely separate BoltDB databases (`containerd`'s `/var/lib/containerd/.../meta.db` vs. Riptide's internal `/var/lib/containerd-gcfs-grpc/metadata.db`). Riptide never touches `containerd`'s BoltDB. However, `containerd` assumes it is the sole client of its configured `[proxy_plugins.gcfs]` gRPC socket. During `containerd`'s periodic GC pass, `containerd` calls `Snapshots.Walk()` over gRPC on Riptide Snapshotter’s sock to list every snapshot stored in Riptide's BoltDB, compares that list against `containerd`'s own `meta.db`, and calls `Snapshots.Remove(key)` over gRPC on any snapshot key in Riptide's BoltDB that `containerd` itself did not create (i.e., Substrate's layers, since Riptide's internal `snapshots/storage` BoltDB bucket is not partitioned by `containerd-namespace`).

&nbsp;

Additionally, in Riptide v2, Riptide Snapshotter delegates `CreateView` and `DeleteView` over `/run/gcfsd/grpc.sock` using the unscoped layer `chainID` hex (`views/<chainID>/fs`) as the view key; sharing the host's `gcfsd` causes `CreateView` collisions (`view "<chainID>" already exists`) for layers already mounted by host `containerd` and causes host `containerd` GC (`DeleteView(<chainID>)`) to unmount `views/<chainID>/fs` out from under Substrate.

&nbsp;

### On-Disk Folder Structure {#on-disk-folder-structure}

&nbsp;

```
/var/lib/ateom-gvisor/
│
├── image-cache/                         <--- 1. LOCAL UNPACK POOL (pause:3.9)
│   ├── version                          (Layout version marker)
│   ├── manifests/
│   │   └── sha256/5678ef01...json       (Image config + ordered diffIDs)
│   └── layers/sha256/
│       └── 11223344.../                 (Content-addressed by layer diffID)
│           ├── fs/                      <-- REAL physical files on host disk
│           │   └── pause
│           ├── whiteouts.json
│           └── finalized
│
├── streaming/                           <--- 2. ADAPTER STREAMING WRAPPERS (agent:v1)
│   └── riptide/
│       └── sha256-abcd1234/
│           ├── lease.json               (Persisted lease state for ReconcileLayers)
│           ├── layer-0/
│           │   ├── fs -> /var/lib/substrate/gcfs/snapshotter/snapshots/101/fs  (Symlink to FUSE)
│           │   └── finalized
│           ├── layer-1/
│           │   ├── fs -> /var/lib/substrate/gcfs/snapshotter/snapshots/102/fs  (Symlink to FUSE)
│           │   └── finalized
│           └── layer-2/
│               ├── fs -> /var/lib/substrate/gcfs/snapshotter/snapshots/103/fs  (Symlink to FUSE)
│               └── finalized
│
└── actors/                              <--- 3. RUNNING ACTOR BUNDLES (Source of Truth)
    ├── actor-pause-001/
    │   └── bundles/pause/
    │       ├── config.json              (OCI container config)
    │       ├── upper/                   (Actor's private writable layer)
    │       ├── work/                    (Overlayfs work directory)
    │       ├── rootfs/                  (Overlayfs mountpoint for runsc)
    │       └── rootfs-overlay.json      <-- OverlaySpec (streamed: false)
    │
    └── actor-agent-002/
        └── bundles/agent/
            ├── config.json
            ├── upper/                   (Actor's private writable layer)
            ├── work/                    (Overlayfs work directory)
            ├── rootfs/                  (Overlayfs mountpoint for runsc)
            └── rootfs-overlay.json      <-- OverlaySpec (streamed: true)

/var/lib/substrate/gcfs/                 <--- 4. ISOLATED RIPTIDE PROVIDER ROOT
├── mnt/views/<chainID>/fs/              (gcfsd-v2 FUSE virtual layer mounts)
├── snapshotter/
│   ├── metadata.db                      (containerd-gcfs-grpc BoltDB)
│   ├── snapshots/<id>/fs -> ../../mnt/views/<chainID>/fs
│   └── layers/                          (On-disk downloaded chunk cache)
└── gcfsd/
    └── images_in_use.db                 (gcfsd-v2 chunk cache metadata DB)
```
